title: Dispositions by department
summary: How each department's requests were closed: released, released in part, withheld, no responsive records, or withdrawn, counted from the agency's own closure notice.

paragraphs: Compare agencies shows, under its ranking, a table of every department with how many of its requests closed each way and that count as a share. The denominator is the department's requests in scope, shown in its own column. The Portal filter above the ranking scopes this table too. Select a count to list its requests; each opens in the inspector.

sections.heading: How a request is counted
paragraphs: Each request is counted once, from the closure notice its portal published (NextRequest portals publish one when a request closes). The first rule whose words appear in the notice decides:
items: Withdrawn: "request withdrawn" or "withdrawn this request", or a request already stored as withdrawn.
No responsive records: "no responsive documents" or "no responsive records".
Withheld: "not released", or "any documents responsive to the request are being withheld".
Released in part: "released except", "released redacted" or "released withheld".

sections.heading: Absence is counted, not guessed
items: Disposition not recorded: no closure notice is stored for the request. It is still open, or it closed without one.
Notice not classified: a notice is stored but no rule matches its wording, or its text has not been extracted yet. Another portal's wording lands here until a rule names it.

sections.heading: What the counts do not say
paragraphs: These are descriptive counts of what each agency answered, not findings. A high share of withheld or no-records closures does not show that any answer was wrong. A department with fewer than 5 requests is marked small, because one request moves its shares by a fifth or more.
